children: Shares of Cohance Lifesciences rose nearly 5.5% on Monday, September 21, after the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) issued a Form 483 containing five observations following an inspection of the company's active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing facility at Jaggaiahpet, Andhra Pradesh.
The inspection was conducted from September 14 to September 19, 2026, according to an exchange filing dated September 21.

The company said the inspection concluded with the issuance of the Form 483 and that it has initiated appropriate corrective and preventive actions (CAPA). Cohance will submit its response within the stipulated timeline and said it remains committed to quality and regulatory compliance.
The company has not disclosed the nature of the five observations in its latest filing.

A Form 483 is issued by USFDA inspectors when they identify conditions or practices that may potentially violate regulatory requirements during an inspection. The observations are shared with the company for review and response and do not by themselves represent a final regulatory action.
Multiple USFDA inspections in recent months
The latest observations come after two other USFDA inspections at Cohance facilities in recent months.

In early September, the company disclosed that its formulation (FDF) facility at Shamshabad, Telangana, had received a Form 483 containing four observations following an inspection conducted from August 27 to September 4. Cohance said it had initiated CAPAs and would respond within the stipulated timeline.

In August, the USFDA had issued five observations following an inspection of Cohance's manufacturing facility at Pashamylaram, Hyderabad, conducted from July 27 to August 5. The company had said those observations were addressable and that none related to data integrity issues. It was preparing a detailed response and CAPAs at the time.

Earlier this month, Cohance Lifesciences announced plans to invest a combined $18 million in NJ Bio and Aruka Bio as it expands its presence in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), a class of targeted cancer treatments.

The company plans to invest $13 million to increase its ownership of NJ Bio and another $5 million in Aruka Bio. Both transactions are to be funded through internal accruals and are subject to definitive agreements, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.

The transactions will give the two businesses separate roles in Cohance's ADC strategy, with NJ Bio focused on research and manufacturing services, while Aruka Bio will focus on developing its own experimental ADC drugs.
Shares of Cohance Lifesciences are trading 5% higher on Monday at ₹460.2. The stock though, is still down 12% on a year-to-date basis, even after having gained over 50% during the last six months.

title: Cohance Lifesciences shares gain over 5% even as Andhra API unit gets five USFDA observations
